requiredFindings.title: Keep the scratch-retention errno field in existing kind K2
requiredFindings.detail: LD-D3A-10 assigns the amended event an errno K3 Errno field. S-OP-2 item 5 defines Errno as K2: a numeric P0 field obtained from raw_os_error(). K3 is RegisteredCode<T>, a registered external text-code match with an unrecognized-text reduction. The product Errno type implements numeric encoding with push_i32 (crates/operability/src/kinds.rs:283-290). Thus the proposed descriptor kind is inconsistent with the actual I/O errno and with the existing-kind ordinary-registration rule. LD-D3A-17 explicitly aligns the amendment with this descriptor and the C-2 kind check, so accepting the amendment as written would accept the wrong field kind.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Change the errno field to K2 Errno, preserving the actual syscall errno, numeric encoding and P0 class. Align the amended required-field inventory, descriptor and C-2 controls with that kind. Keep reason as K1 ScratchRetainedReason and errno present exactly for io-failure, absent for work-exhausted; no new kind or synthetic errno is needed.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Do not use artifact modification order as proof of the build invocation
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Reading the exact supervisor_fixture compiler-artifact executable path removes directory-scan ambiguity, and the harmless standalone entry resolves the prior startup question. However fixture mtime >= test-executable mtime does not prove that the path file was written by the current invocation. A stale path file and unchanged executables can pass it on a later filtered run; a valid build can reuse an older cached fixture while rebuilding the test executable and fail it. The claimed automatic rejection of every invocation that did not build the fixture does not follow.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestedChange: Make the build-and-run wrapper own this association explicitly: consume the artifact records from the successful current build, refresh or invalidate its path handoff, and run the exact test artifacts selected by that build. Define direct Cargo runs without that wrapper as unsupported or provide an explicit invocation binding; do not present mtime ordering as proof. This remains a test-lane reliability observation, not a production authority gap.
